exemptions.reason: Leaflet's own bundled zoom stack (+/− at its vendor font-size), "Find my location" locate button, and the scale bar are third-party chrome — docs/DESIGN.md's radius section (Documented exceptions #4) already carries the zoom-stack/locate-button radius override and the scale-bar non-exception as the accepted boundary of what this token scale reaches. Their child <a>/<div> nodes are deliberately radius:0 BY THE APP'S OWN CSS (the rounded corner the user sees comes from the parent .leaflet-bar container's overflow:hidden clip, not the button), so a per-button override here would fight the exact mechanism that already unified their visible shape with the app's own RADIUS.md. The one thing left off-scale (the zoom glyphs' 22px font) is Leaflet's own vendor CSS (.leaflet-touch .leaflet-control-zoom-in/-out), not an app literal.

AppHeader.jsx's wordmark/logo button (title "Dashboard: all projects") paints no border and no background (background:transparent, border:none) — it is a hit-target around the BrandMark, not a visible chip. Nothing renders for the eye to compare against another shape, so it is not the kind of drift this budget exists to bound. Giving it a real chip's chrome (a border/fill it has never had) to make its signature merge would ADD visible clutter around the logo — the opposite of the ask — so it stays a documented, permanent exception rather than a value change.

note: HARD BUDGET for ui-audit/ui-inventory.mjs's per-surface DISTINCT CONTROL SIGNATURE count (NEW-1, B1038016) — supersedes the old ratchet-only control-signature-ceiling.json (B982402), which only ever forbade a surface's count from GROWING past whatever it happened to measure the day it was written and so could never force a real reduction. A surface's raw signature count must be <= bySurface[surface] + the sum of every exemption's `count` that names that surface (see `effectiveCeiling` in ui-inventory.mjs) — exemptions ADD to the ceiling, they never subtract from the reported raw count, and every exemption is printed on every run, pass or fail. Regenerate a surface's OWN bySurface number only by hand, after a session genuinely lowers it through real control convergence (or, for a first-time surface, a first honest measurement) — never edit it to silence a real regression, and never add an exemption for a signature that a real code fix could remove instead. Every number here was set from a real post-fix measurement — see BACKLOG.md B1038016 for the per-surface reasoning and what was converged to reach it. CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (x2): "Map landing page (comp mode)" 15->16 and "Map landing page (selecting parcels)" 17->18. FIRST correction: the ORIGINAL 2026-09-01 numbers were measured from this repo's Claude Code sandbox, whose egress proxy allowlists only a few hosts and cannot reach Supabase or any of the real county/statewide ArcGIS hosts this crawl's landing view tries — so CompsPanel.jsx's "+ New comps"/"Import (KML)" buttons (gated `!loading && !loadError`, behind a real Supabase fetchAllComps() call) and MapFinder.jsx's selection-guidance tooltip (data-testid="select-parcels-tip", gated `!err`, cleared by a real county-GIS parcel-layer fetch succeeding) never rendered in the sandbox, while real CI (a GitHub Actions runner with normal network access) measured one more signature on each, deterministically (run 33581085858, job 100095330406, reproduced identically across three separate runs). SECOND correction (same day, same items): a raised budget number alone left the underlying crawl still environment-dependent, so docs/UI-INVENTORY.md (which embeds the raw counts as text) could never be regenerated byte-identically between this sandbox and CI — `--check`'s literal diff against the committed file would fail forever from here. Root-caused precisely (confirmed via curl: Supabase and every county GIS host this crawl reaches are blocked with a fast 403 from the sandbox's own proxy in well under a second, so no wait time could ever bridge it) and fixed at the source: `ui-inventory.mjs`'s `mockExternalNetwork` now intercepts every external request for these two surfaces and fulfills it with a generic, minimally-valid SUCCESSFUL response, so both surfaces settle to the identical rendered state (verified byte-for-byte against CI's own captured output) in every environment, deterministically. The counts above (16/18, effective ceiling 20/22) are therefore the real, permanently reproducible measurement, not a one-time CI snapshot.
